accounting.rationale: Original PDF125 lines33-34 defines the nonallocatable nonpointer dummy-array category and its effective-argument shape. The actual extent/bound effect is accounted under p4, not a separate no-op definition program.
An ALLOCATABLE dummy declared with colons has a different category; a valid deferred-shape declaration is not an invalid assumed-shape declaration merely because its spelling is similar.
Array pointers use their own association and deferred-shape rules. Do not transfer ordinary dummy lower-bound defaults to a pointer dummy.
PENDING complete dummy/actual and explicit-interface source context under15.4.2.2 and15.5.2.5, not an ordinary local colon declaration.
The array category requires nonzero rank. Scalar entities reached through a zero-size bound vector or RANK(0) retain their actual category and inquiry restrictions.
Shape derives from the effective argument, not necessarily its lower bounds. The runtime p4 requirement retains the complete association premises; no copying or ABI mechanism is promised.
PDF125 line35 has a required colon and optional scalar lower-bound, whose canonical specification-expression definition remains R816.
PDF125 line36 is one explicit-bounds-expr followed by a colon, not a list that mixes a vector with additional scalar shape entries.
PDF126 lines1-3 gives guarded rank determination followed by scalar/array classification. The latter is not an extra executable classifier.
Nonzero established rank gives an assumed-shape array. Total size can still be zero.
A bound vector of size zero establishes a scalar, unlike a rank-one vector containing a zero lower bound. Do not impose array-only inquiry arguments on the scalar.
PDF126 lines4-5 retains the vector, otherwise scalar, otherwise one alternatives and their dimension scope.
PDF126 lines6-8 specifies corresponding extents and the upper-bound relation. UBOUND/LBOUND have additional whole-array and empty-dimension result rules.

requirements.title: A scalar assumed-shape specification has an optional lower bound and a colon
requirements.definition: The scalar assumed-shape-spec is a colon with an optional preceding lower-bound. R816 defines that bound as a scalar integer specification expression. The list form and the R821 bound-vector form are different R814 alternatives, and the entity's attributes and role determine whether a colon declaration is assumed shape or deferred shape.

pending.omitted-lower: PENDING a complete explicit-interface procedure with a nonpointer nonallocatable INTEGER dummy x(:), and a conforming defined rank-one actual. Compile/admission is not a runtime lower-bound or extent observation.
pending.specified-scalar-lower: PENDING the same genuine dummy context with x(-2:) and with a prior nonoptional non-INTENT(OUT) INTEGER bound dummy satisfying10.1.11. Negative lower bounds are permitted, not diagnostic cases.
pending.expression-and-alternative-source: PENDING an exact R816/C1011 source relation for a noninteger or nonrestricted scalar lower-bound candidate and a minimally repaired valid control. Exclude valid R821 vector parses and R814 explicit/deferred/assumed-size alternatives before assigning a grammar error. Keep one canonical owner rather than duplicate lower-bound negatives.

requirements.oracle: Complete scalar assumed-shape admissions and narrowly scoped expression/grammar relations. Any future negative needs a source-specific predicate and minimal repair, not an intended parse that another valid production can replace.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Numbered reporting capability does not mandate fatal rejection, English text or a printed rule code. Unsupported features, generic expected/constant/kind strings, source echoes, ICE/verifier failures and wrong-source recovery do not prove the intended condition.

requirements.title: A vector assumed-shape specification is a bound expression followed by a colon
requirements.definition: The assumed-shape-bounds-spec has one explicit-bounds-expr followed by a colon. R819/C833 give its integer, restricted-expression, rank-one and constant-size premises. Its values need not be constant and its size can be zero. It is not a component-array-spec alternative under R740.

pending.vector-lower-bounds: PENDING an ordinary INTEGER dummy x(lower:) in a complete explicit interface, with a prior fixed-size rank-one INTEGER lower vector and a same-rank actual. Use a two-element constant vector and a restricted dummy vector whose values vary across separate valid calls, without changing expected values from an affected descriptor.
pending.zero-size-vector-boundary: PENDING a prior rank-one INTEGER constant vector of size0 and the resulting scalar dummy, supplied with a defined scalar actual through an explicit interface. A vector containing one zero element instead specifies rank1 with lower bound0. No array-only inquiry on the ordinary scalar.
pending.bound-expression-contract: PENDING exact canonical R819/C833 rank/type/restricted/constant-size negative-and-repair relations and R814 alternative parsing. Do not mix one vector-bounds-spec with additional scalar list entries, expand R740 component grammar, or duplicate the canonical expression cases. These F2023 forms are not optional capability skips.

requirements.oracle: Finite complete vector-bound admissions, with rank and lower-bound run/effect plans under the corresponding prose requirements. Expression diagnostics retain their original causal predicates and owners.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A scalar bound may select R820 and is not automatically a malformed vector. No bound-value constancy requirement, positive-size requirement, fixed kind ID or compiler-consensus oracle is introduced.

requirements.title: Without a RANK clause, list length or bound-vector size establishes rank
requirements.source: 8.5.8.3 p2 rank-determination clauses, physical PDF126, lines1-3
requirements.definition: When a rank-clause does not specify rank, the rank comes from the number of colons in the assumed-shape-spec-list or the size of the vector in assumed-shape-bounds-spec. The vector-size route can establish rank zero. Zero total array size does not reduce a nonzero established rank.

pending.list-rank: PENDING a run/effect using actual dummy x(:,:) with a defined rank-two INTEGER actual of shape[3,2]; require direct RANK(x)=2 and that ordered shape, not RANK of a constructor or a fixed-rank observer destination.
pending.vector-rank: PENDING actual dummy x(lower:) where lower has constant size2 and the actual has shape[3,2]. Require literal rank2 and shape[3,2], independently of lower vector values or its own declared index origin.
pending.zero-vector-scalar: PENDING a complete call using a constant zero-size lower vector: assign/read a defined scalar value through the dummy, require direct RANK=0 and a rank-one empty SHAPE result. Do not use SIZE/LBOUND/UBOUND directly on that ordinary scalar.
pending.rank-clause-source: PENDING the canonical R829/C863/C864 and8.5.17p2 relation. This guard does not establish local colon-count evidence when RANK specifies rank. Any admission-only S-facet use needs approved role support; do not use the unintegrated positive_control_facets field or retag a positive control as a runtime effect.

requirements.oracle: Direct actual-dummy rank and legal shape/value observations with literal expectations. Nonzero and zero-rank outcomes are meaningful property checks, not count-filling declaration-only programs.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Complete type/kind/rank, definability and explicit-interface premises apply. A source/role gate stays pending; no compile-only substitute for the stated run/effect plans, scalar/array shortcut, or corank proxy.

requirements.title: Assumed-shape lower bounds come from the vector, scalar specifications or default one
requirements.definition: A present explicit-bounds-expr supplies lower bounds for every dimension. Otherwise each specified scalar lower-bound supplies its dimension's bound, with one for an omitted lower bound. These are dummy bounds, not an unconditional copy of effective-argument lower bounds. Inquiry normalization remains separate from the declared values.

pending.omitted-defaults: PENDING a defined whole INTEGER actual t(-2:0,4:5) passed to dummy x(:,:). Inside require LBOUND(x)=[1,1], UBOUND(x)=[3,2], SHAPE(x)=[3,2], using literal expectations rather than copying the actual's nonunit lower bounds.
pending.specified-scalar-lowers: PENDING the same shape[3,2] actual with dummy x(0:,-3:). Require lower[0,-3] and upper[2,-2], with defined dimension-specific data. Scalar bound data must satisfy prior typing and restricted specification-expression premises.
pending.mixed-list-defaults: PENDING dummy x(0:,:) with that actual, expecting lower[0,1] and upper[2,2]. Handle the omitted bound per dimension, not as a global scalar/vector broadcast.
pending.vector-ordinal-lowers: PENDING dummy x(lower:) with the two-element vector values[-5,7], including a vector declared with a different index origin. Expect lower[-5,7], upper[-3,8], shape[3,2]. Use ordinal element-to-dimension correspondence and independent literal results.
pending.zero-extent-inquiry-boundary: PENDING a shape[0,4] actual with dummy lower values[5,-2]. Declared upper values follow[4,1], but legal whole-dummy queries return LBOUND=[1,-2] and UBOUND=[0,1]. Do not read an element or force the normalized first-dimension inquiry to echo its declared bound.

requirements.oracle: Run/effect observations on the actual dummy object, with complete argument contexts and literal nonempty/empty-dimension expectations. No actual-descriptor, TRANSFER or address-based self-oracle.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Whole arrays differ from expressions/sections under9.5.2 and the inquiry rules. Overall zero size does not normalize every dimension. Pointer/allocatable dummies are not this category, and scalar zero-vector entities cannot be fed to ordinary array-only inquiries.

requirements.title: Effective-argument extents and the dummy lower bound determine the upper bound
requirements.definition: Each dimension of an assumed-shape dummy has the extent of the corresponding effective-argument dimension. With dummy lower bound d and effective extent s, the upper bound is s+d-1. This does not promise actual/dummy address identity, a copying mechanism or unconditional equality between the declared upper bound and UBOUND's normalized empty-dimension result.

pending.whole-actual-extents: PENDING a complete explicit-interface run with an actual shape[3,2], checking the dummy's direct SHAPE=[3,2] and SIZE=6 and defined data in dimension order. All expected values are independently literal, not obtained from another affected descriptor.
pending.section-effective-extent: PENDING a defined parent INTEGER vector of five elements with values11 through15 and its nonvector section1:5:2 passed to a dummy with lower -1. Require extent3, lower -1, upper1 and values[11,13,15]; the parent extent5 is not the effective section extent. Do not test copying, addresses or IS_CONTIGUOUS here.
pending.nonempty-upper-relation: PENDING dummy lower[-5,7] with effective extents[3,2], expecting literal upper[-3,8]. Do not merely compare two expressions computed from the same possibly incorrect dummy descriptor.
pending.empty-extent-effect: PENDING a valid shape[0,4] effective argument: rank2, shape[0,4] and total0 persist for the dummy. Apply the separate per-dimension LBOUND/UBOUND rules, and perform no payload access.
pending.interface-and-contiguity-source: PENDING exact15.5.2.5 rank/type/kind, assumed-size exclusion, definability and vector-subscript restrictions plus CONTIGUOUS/C1548/C1549 contexts. C715_valid__contiguous is a preserved run/positive-control for its own intrinsic-argument condition, not a measured shape/bound effect here. Do not clone it, promote its role, or import unsupported role metadata.

requirements.oracle: Real run/effect checks of the actual dummy's extents, qualified bounds and defined data. The actual argument must satisfy its complete association/interface contract; permitted noncontiguous actuals do not imply a specified temporary strategy.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No mandatory diagnostic or invalid-program twin is invented for this pure effect. A source/role gate remains pending, while required runtime behavior cannot be replaced with compile-only success or an optional-capability skip.
